1320 is a leap year (divisible by 4 and 400? 1320 mod 400 = 320, but rule before Gregorian reform: Julian calendar in use then; for historical dates we treat as proleptic Gregorian per instructions? The problem says "Use Gregorian calendar arithmetic," so we apply Gregorian rules even for 1320).  
1320 is divisible by 4: yes.  
Divisible by 100: yes (1320/100=13.2? Wait 1320/100=13.2? No, 1320/100=13.2 means not integer? Actually 100*13=1300, remainder 20, so 1320/100=13.2, but that's not integer division. 1320 mod 100 = 20, so not divisible by 100. So leap year under Gregorian: divisible by 4 and not divisible by 100 unless divisible by 400. 1320 mod 100 ≠ 0, so leap year.  

Start date: 1320-01-11 (assuming format 11-01-1320 is DD-MM-YYYY).  
Subtract 57 days:  
January has 31 days.  
From Jan 11 back 11 days → Jan 1.  
Remaining days to subtract: 57 - 11 = 46 days.  
Now before Jan 1: go into December 1319.  
December 1319 has 31 days.  
46 - 31 = 15 days left.  
Now into November 1319.  
November has 30 days.  
We go back 15 days from Dec 1 (which is Nov 30, Nov 29, ...).  
From Dec 1 back 1 day → Nov 30. Back 15 days → Nov 30 - 14 days = Nov 16.  
Check: 15 days before Dec 1 is Nov 16 (Nov 16 to Nov 30 = 15 days inclusive? Actually from Nov 16 to Nov 30 = 15 days, so Dec 1 minus 15 days = Nov 16).  

Thus final date: 1319-11-16.  

FINAL_ANSWER: 1319-11-16
